observation_summary: The verification process failed when a mock call was nested within another mock call in the same line, because the verification logic was incorrectly triggered for the wrong mock.
reasoning_summary: The fix introduces a guard condition (`if (verificationMode instanceof MockAwareVerificationMode && ((MockAwareVerificationMode) verificationMode).getMock() == invocation.getMock())`) to ensure that verification only proceeds if the mock being verified matches the mock associated with the verification mode. This is a classic missing guard/validation check on the execution path.
evidence_used: The fix adds a conditional check in MockHandler.java to verify the mock instance before proceeding with verification.
The fix wraps the verification mode in a MockAwareVerificationMode in MockitoCore.java to carry the necessary context for the check.
The bug report and stack trace indicate that verification was failing when multiple mock calls were involved in the same line, implying the system was incorrectly attempting to verify the wrong mock.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix involves changing how the verification mode is passed (a change in the interface/contract of the verification process), the root cause is the lack of a check to ensure the verification is applied to the correct mock instance, which is a validation/guard issue.
